name: History of Technology in Modern Times II
description:
At the turn of the 19th century, a new historical epoch began that has lasted to this day: modernity. It is characterized by a historically unique speed of social, technical and cultural change as well as population and economic growth. Societies' self-descriptions, their relationships to space and time, and their relationship to nature and technology are changing.

Modernism is an important epoch for us because it reaches into the present. This course is part of a two-semester cycle on the history of technology. The lecture in this winter semester continues the lecture on the history of technology in the 19th century (summer semester 2022), but it can also be attended if you did not attended part one.

The focus is on the history of art and culture in the early 20th century, the history of rationalization and computerization, the Cold War and the use of nuclear energy and (global) infrastructure.
